REVISE — limited exposition and dependency repairsThe all-parameter two-leg theorem, the degree-sensitive local lemma, and the conditional ownership extension pass the mathematical checks below. I found no counterexample to any of the five assertions of the two-leg theorem, including for unequal even leg lengths and arbitrary mixed promotion bundles.My revision recommendation has two specific grounds:A sentence in §4 is literally false: “All remaining tips are blank.” For  $(w,a,b)=(6,6,4)$ , an admissible candidate tip is selected. It still fails the required endpoint condition, so this is an exposition error with a one-sentence repair.The requested exhaustive check of the old22 example cannot be completed from the supplied package. The two displayed local exclusions are correct, but the referenced 22-endpoint configuration and complete four-anchor list are absent. The supplied earlier configuration has 20 endpoints, and cannot substitute for old22.The review below distinguishes these issues from the substantive proofs that work. References are to sections of the supplied notes. I have not executed the checkers or Lean files, and I do not treat their reported execution as independently established evidence.1. Construction, matching, and feasibility for unequal legsWrite
$$w=2k,\qquad a=2\alpha,\qquad b=2\beta,\qquad
S=\alpha+\beta,$$
where  $k\ge3$  and  $\alpha,\beta\ge2$ .The matching covers every endpoint exactly onceThe matching in §1 partitions the endpoint set into four disjoint portions:PortionMatching edgesNumberUpper bar row $(0,j)(0,j+1)$ ,  $j$  odd $k$ Lower bar interior $(1,j)(1,j+1)$ ,  $j=2,4,\ldots,w-2$  $k-1$ Left leg, including its lower bar corner $(r,1)(r+1,1)$ ,  $r=1,3,\ldots,a-1$  $\alpha$ Right leg, including its lower bar corner $(r,w)(r+1,w)$ ,  $r=1,3,\ldots,b-1$  $\beta$ Consequently,
$$|M|=2k+S-1=w+S-1,
\qquad
|P|=2(w+S-1).$$
The two lower bar corners are covered by the vertical leg edges, so they are neither omitted nor covered twice.Every selection has exactly one occupied neighborFor a leg of height  $h$ , each selection has the following unique occupied neighbor:The upper support sees the corresponding upper bar corner.An even-row exterior support sees the endpoint in that row of the leg.An odd-row interior support sees the endpoint in that row of the leg.The bottom support  $(h+1,c)$  sees  $(h,c)$ .The possible interactions that require checking are harmless:Consecutive side supports alternate between the exterior and interior columns, so they are not adjacent.The first interior support occurs in row  $3$ . Its north neighbor is in row  $2$ , outside the two-row bar.The two interior-support columns are  $2$  and  $w-1$ , separated by  $w-3\ge3$ .The bottom support of a shorter leg has blank neighbors below and to its sides. The taller opposite leg is too far away to introduce another occupied neighbor.Thus the proof does not require  $a=b$ . Each leg contributes  $h+1$  selections, yielding
$$|T|=(a+1)+(b+1)=2S+2.$$
Occupied degree and connectivityThe endpoint classification in §2 is exhaustive:Endpoint typeOccupied neighborsBar interiorThree bar endpointsUpper bar cornerTwo endpoints and one selectionLower bar cornerUpper, inward, and downward endpointsInterior leg endpointTwo vertical endpoints and one side selectionBottom leg endpointOne endpoint, its exterior selection, and its bottom selectionEvery endpoint therefore has occupied degree exactly three. Both legs attach to the connected bar, so  $H=P$  is one complete connected endpoint component.Finding: assertion 1 is correct throughout the stated parameter range.2. The freezing order is complete and excludes all mixed bundlesThe prose order in §2 works. Explicit indexing makes its completeness and the earlier-mate relationships particularly clear.Even leg verticesFor a leg in column  $c$ , freeze
$$(h,c),(h-2,c),\ldots,(2,c).$$
The actual mate of  $(r,c)$  is  $(r-1,c)$ . Its witnesses are its exterior selection and  $(r+1,c)$ .At  $r=h$ , the latter is the bottom selection. Otherwise,
$$(r+1,c)=m(r+2,c),$$
and  $(r+2,c)$  has already been frozen. The witnesses are distinct adjacent vertices, neither equal to the vertex’s own mate.The two legs can be processed independently, in either order.First bar waveDefine
$$U_j=(\varepsilon_j,j),\qquad 1\le j\le w-1,$$
where  $\varepsilon_j=0$  for odd  $j$ , and  $\varepsilon_j=1$  for even  $j$ . Process
$$U_1,U_2,\ldots,U_{w-1}.$$
The actual matching gives
$$m(U_j)=(\varepsilon_j,j+1).$$
The first vertex  $U_1=(0,1)$  uses the selection  $(0,0)$  and
$$(1,1)=m(2,1).$$
For  $j\ge2$ , its vertical witness is
$$(1-\varepsilon_j,j)=m(U_{j-1}).$$
Its west witness is  $m(2,1)$  when  $j=2$ , and for  $j\ge3$  is
$$(\varepsilon_j,j-1)=m(U_{j-2}).$$
Every dependency therefore points strictly earlier in the prescribed order.Opposite bar waveDefine
$$V_j=(\delta_j,j),\qquad 2\le j\le w,$$
where
$$\delta_j=(w-j)\bmod2=j\bmod2,$$
using the evenness of  $w$ . Process
$$V_w,V_{w-1},\ldots,V_2.$$
Here
$$m(V_j)=(\delta_j,j-1).$$
The initial vertex  $V_w=(0,w)$  uses  $(0,w+1)\in T$  and
$$(1,w)=m(2,w).$$
Subsequently, the vertical witness is  $m(V_{j+1})$ . The east witness is  $m(2,w)$  at the first subsequent step, and otherwise  $m(V_{j+2})$ .At each common column,  $U_j$  and  $V_j$  occupy opposite rows. The waves are therefore disjoint, and together cover every upper bar endpoint and every lower interior bar endpoint.Lower corners and remaining odd leg verticesThe lower-left corner has witnesses
$$(0,1)=m(V_2),\qquad (1,2)=m(V_3).$$
The lower-right corner has witnesses
$$(0,w)=m(U_{w-1}),\qquad
(1,w-1)=m(U_{w-2}).$$
All four indices exist for the stated widths.Finally, an odd leg vertex  $(r,c)$ , with  $r=3,5,\ldots,h-1$ , uses its interior selection and
$$(r-1,c)=m(r-2,c).$$
For  $r=3$ , the earlier endpoint is the lower bar corner. Thereafter it is the preceding odd leg vertex in this final sequence.The total number of ordered endpoints is
$$S+(w-1)+(w-1)+2+(S-2)
=2(w+S-1)=|P|.$$
The portions are disjoint, so every endpoint appears exactly once.Why the argument covers arbitrary mixed promotionsLet  $E$  be a nonempty proposed promotion bundle under the stipulated operation: original selections remain occupied, and deleting an original endpoint requires promoting its actual mate. Choose the earliest member  $v\in E$  in the order above.Each witness of  $v$  is either:an original selection, which remains occupied; or $m(u)$  for an earlier endpoint  $u$ , which cannot be deleted because that would require  $u\in E$ .Thus  $v$ , after promotion, still has two distinct occupied neighbors. This contradicts selected-vertex feasibility.No checkerboard direction is used in this argument. Nor does it depend on enumerating bundles.Finding: assertion 2 is correct. The freezing proof is genuinely an all-parameter, all-bundle proof.3. \{Q_{0,j}:0\le j\le k\}

$$Q_{\alpha,0},\qquad Q_{\beta,k}.$$
It follows that
$$|R_H|=k+1+S,\qquad
|T\cap R_H|=S+4,\qquad
|\text{blanks in }R_H|=S+2.$$

The actual mate of the bottom-right endpoint is

Hence the two stated saturated-endpoint corrections are exactly
$$Q_{\alpha,0}\longrightarrow Q_{\alpha-1,0},
\qquad
Q_{\beta,k}\longrightarrow Q_{\beta-1,k},$$
each transferring  $1/2$ .The resulting corrected ledger is therefore:TileCorrected charge $Q_{\alpha-1,0}$  $1/2$  $Q_{\beta-1,k}$  $1/2$ Every other receiver tile, including both bottom tiles $0$ The destination tiles exist and are distinct. Both transfers remain inside the same complete receiver, also when  $a\ne b$ . Thus
$$\rho_H
=(S+4)+(2k+S-1)-2(k+1+S)
=1.$$
This supplies the individual transfer check that is only described verbally in §3. The corrected total is not obtained by pretending that each raw tile excess is already its corrected charge.Finding: assertion 3 is correct under the supplied original correction convention. Adding the two destination coordinates would improve the exposition.Full-grid ledgerLet  $H_{\max}=\max(a,b)$ . The rectangle has dimensions
$$(H_{\max}+2)\times(w+2),$$
and
$$|T|+|M|=w+3S+1.$$
Therefore
$$\Delta
=\frac{(H_{\max}+2)(w+2)}2-(w+3S+1)
=\frac{H_{\max}(w+2)}2-3S+1.$$
Since  $S\le H_{\max}$ ,
$$\Delta\ge \frac{H_{\max}(w-4)}2+1>0.$$
One can also check the outside deficit directly. There are
$$\frac{H_{\max}}2(k+1)-S$$
endpoint-free tiles and  $S-2$  selections outside the receiver. Consequently,
$$D_{\mathrm{all}}
=H_{\max}(k+1)-3S+2
=\Delta+1.$$
Thus the original identity reads exactly
$$\Delta=D_{\mathrm{all}}-\rho_H.$$
For  $w=6$ ,  $a=b=4$ , these formulas give the stated objective  $19$ , outside deficit  $6$ , and total deficit  $5$ .4.
